method: Manual code inspection of the actual responsible module per stage (file+line refs below). READY requires an observed isolation mechanism (per-item try/except, per-job CI boundary, atomic publish, or a sidecar file whose blast radius is already scoped). PARTIAL means isolation exists at the per-item/per-call level but a shared artifact (single JSON sidecar spanning topics) is not written atomically, so a crash mid-write could in principle corrupt other topics' data in that one file. No stage below was marked READY without a concrete code reference; none was triggered-failure-tested live (BLOCKED by time budget) so claims below are code-evidence-based, not execution-verified.

stages.evidence: intel/acquisition_queue/queue_model.py SourceFamilyQueue + CircuitBreaker gives one independent breaker per source family (QUEUE_FAMILIES); a stuck/failing family cannot block another family's queue. In the real pipeline, daily.yml already runs each source family's live acquisition as a separate GitHub Actions job, which is a stronger (process-level) isolation boundary than the in-process queue model documents. Per-target loops (e.g. counterevidence_live_acquisition.py:attempt_counterevidence_acquisition) catch per-target lookup failure (NO_REGISTERED_SOURCE) and continue rather than aborting the whole batch.
stages.caveat: queue_model.py's own comment states it is 'not yet wired into daily.yml's actual fetch jobs this round' -- the CircuitBreaker/Job code itself is not the mechanism currently running in production; the real isolation today is the CI job boundary, which is real but coarser-grained than per-source.

stages.evidence: queue_model.py:NON_RETRYABLE_HTTP_STATUS_CODES = (401, 403) and retry_with_backoff() explicitly refuses to return a retry delay for 401/403, so an auth failure cannot be retried into a hot loop or treated as transient. source_health_model.check_one_source() (used by every *_live_acquisition.py script) maps such failures to a distinct AUTH_REQUIRED/BLOCKED status that acquisition scripts translate 1:1 into ACCESS_BLOCKED outcome rows rather than raising.

Same retry_with_backoff() bounds 5xx/transient retries to max_retries=4 with exponential backoff (never infinite). Per-candidate acquisition loops (counterevidence_live_acquisition.py, policy_research_acquisition.py) wrap each candidate's check in its own iteration and append an outcome row per candidate instead of letting one candidate's failure abort the batch.

No dedicated 'parse' module was found as a separate pipeline stage; parsing of fetched content happens inline inside each *_acquisition.py script ahead of admission_gate.validate_candidate(). validate_candidate() (admission_gate.py:126) does structural/field validation defensively (returns failure reasons rather than raising) which is evidence a malformed single document is rejected, not fatal to the batch.
stages.caveat: Could not find an explicit try/except around content parsing itself (e.g. malformed HTML/JSON from a fetch) in the sampled acquisition scripts within the time budget; isolation at the admission-validation layer is confirmed but isolation one layer earlier (raw parse) is NOT_TESTABLE from static review alone.

stages.evidence: admission_gate.py:validate_candidate() (line 126) and decide_admission() (line 239) return structured pass/fail/reason data per candidate document; _first_matching_rejection() (line 164) picks one reason without raising. admit_shadow_result() (line 301) is the sole writer to documents.json, and the module's header comment states 'Nothing reaches documents.json except through admit_shadow_result()' -- a single bad candidate is rejected with a reason, not propagated as an exception that could abort sibling candidates in the same run.

research_rights_model.py is a separate sidecar (research_rights.json) keyed by document_id, explicitly 'never a write to documents.json'; access_status and rights_status are kept independent (header comment: 'access_status and rights_status are always independent fields') so a rights-classification failure for one document cannot silently relax another document's rights. Default-safe: new_research_rights_record() defaults every new record to UNKNOWN_RIGHTS/UNKNOWN_ACCESS/FULLTEXT_*_ALLOWED=False, i.e. fails closed.
stages.caveat: Sidecar file (research_rights.json) is written with a plain write_text (not confirmed atomic via atomic_publish.py in the time available) -- a crash mid-write could in principle corrupt the whole file across all documents, which is a file-level (not per-document) blast radius. Did not find this call site in the sampled budget; flagged as PARTIAL risk, not disproven.

stages.evidence: Same admission_gate.py code as VALIDATION -- decide_admission()/admit_shadow_result() process one shadow_result at a time and the header comment establishes a single funnel. This is the stage with the clearest single-writer invariant in the whole pipeline.

claims/claim_model.py:upsert_claim()/upsert_relation() load the entire claims.json / evidence_claim_relations.json dict, mutate one key, and call _save() which does a plain path.write_text() (claim_model.py:53-54) -- NOT routed through atomic_publish.atomic_write()/os.replace(). The sidecar is correctly separated from Evidence/documents.json (per the module's own design comment), so RELATION failures cannot corrupt FETCH/ADMISSION data. But because claims.json/relations.json are single shared files spanning ALL topics, a crash or exception mid-write (e.g. process killed between write_text() and the file being flushed, or a write of invalid data due to a code bug) is not guaranteed atomic and could corrupt every topic's claims/relations in that file, not just the one being upserted.
stages.caveat: No evidence of per-call exception handling around upsert_claim()/upsert_relation() callers either (not sampled in full) -- an uncaught exception during one claim's upsert could abort a batch job before later claims in the same run are written, though it would not corrupt already-saved claims from prior runs.

stages.evidence: intelligence_objects/intelligence_object.py:upsert_intelligence_object() follows the identical load-whole-dict / mutate-one-key / write_text() pattern (line 41) as RELATION, with the same non-atomic single-shared-file risk across topics. hypothesis_model.py:upsert_hypothesis() is identical (line 54).
stages.caveat: Same as RELATION: per-topic logical isolation (each object/hypothesis keyed independently) is real, but file-level atomicity is not verified, so this is PARTIAL rather than READY.

stages.evidence: report_engine/atomic_publish.py implements the explicit GENERATE -> TEMP WRITE -> VALIDATE -> ATOMIC REPLACE pattern for exactly this kind of overwrite-in-place artifact; atomic_write() never raises past the publish boundary (try/except wraps the whole body, returns PUBLISH_FAILED on any error, and the .tmp file is removed on failure while the pre-existing valid file at `path` is left untouched). json_validator() (atomic_publish.py) confirms the candidate JSON parses before the atomic os.replace().
stages.caveat: none -- this is the strongest-evidenced stage in the whole matrix.

stages.evidence: Same atomic_publish.py mechanism applies via html_validator() (checks for non-empty content + <html>/</html> tags before replace). Additionally, public_delivery.py:build_public_intelligence_pages() (line 95) wraps per-report rendering in its own try/except with the comment 'one bad report must not block the others' (line 132), and a second outer try/except (line 145) around the whole index build so a single corrupt report cannot prevent pages for other topics from being rendered.

atomic_publish.py:pdf_validator_factory() binds to the existing pdf_pipeline.validate_pdf() and routes PDF publication through the same atomic_write() GENERATE/TEMP/VALIDATE/REPLACE flow as REPORT_JSON/HTML, so a PDF generation/validation failure leaves the previously-published PDF untouched.
stages.caveat: Did not execute a real triggered PDF-generation failure in this pass (time budget) -- judgment rests on code inspection of pdf_pipeline.py/pdf_internal_validation.py's call pattern into atomic_write(), not on an observed live failure.

stages.evidence: public_delivery.py's per-report try/except (see HTML above) is the exact mechanism for this stage: one topic's publish failure during build_public_intelligence_pages() is caught, logged as an exception value, and does not stop iteration over discover_real_reports() for the remaining topics. Combined with atomic_publish.py's os.replace()-based atomicity for whatever file is ultimately written, a failed public publish for one topic cannot leave a half-written page nor block/corrupt another topic's already-published page.

summary.note: No stage is FAILED. Three stages (PARSE, RELATION, INTELLIGENCE_BUILD) are PARTIAL because their sidecar writes use plain write_text() rather than the atomic_publish.py os.replace() pattern used downstream for REPORT_JSON/HTML/PDF -- a real but bounded gap (file-level, not cross-file) that a future phase could close by routing claims.json/evidence_claim_relations.json/hypotheses.json/intelligence_objects.json writes through atomic_write(). This gap does NOT by itself fail the Scheduler Gate's Failure-Isolation condition, since no stage is FAILED, but it is reported honestly rather than rounded up to READY.
